component.name: Apache Traffic Server
component.description: Caching HTTP proxy server. The security policy follows the ASF vulnerability handling process; its security model states that administrative users are trusted, that experimental features (explicitly including HTTP/3 and QUIC support) are not treated as security surfaces, and that plugins shipped with Traffic Server, including those under plugins/experimental/, are in scope for security reporting.

externalReferences.comment: Source security model document; this file is a structured translation of it.

threats.name: Vulnerability in a plugin shipped with Traffic Server
threats.description: Plugins shipped with Traffic Server, including those under plugins/experimental/, are in scope for security reporting; vulnerabilities in them should be reported through the private security mailing list following the ASF process.

threats.name: Attacks requiring administrative access
threats.description: Administrative users are always considered to be trusted; reports where an attacker already has access to or control over Traffic Server binaries and/or scripts, or Traffic Server configuration files, are rejected.

threats.name: Vulnerability in an experimental feature (including HTTP/3 and QUIC)
threats.description: Experimental features are known unstable and not supposed to be used in production; vulnerabilities in them are not considered security issues. This explicitly includes HTTP/3 and QUIC support, which remain experimental. Such issues may be reported publicly, though the project asks to be contacted privately for serious or uncertain cases.

threats.name: Disclosure of security-sensitive information through modified logging
threats.description: Security-sensitive information may be logged with modified logging configurations, particularly if debug logging is enabled; this is an operator configuration consequence, not a Traffic Server vulnerability.
